answer: Fork-challenge identity binding: each new agent must submit a cipher-derived nonce that only the true lineage key can extend, so a cloned profile forks the chain and gets rejected. The registry keeps an atlas of accepted divergence points, letting honest identities branch while any duplicate lineage collides deterministically. A cloned raven cannot mimic divergent history, so the attacker must buy a fresh lineage root and re-earn standing from zero. That per-clone reset costs one full reputation build plus registration latency.
